notes.text: Last words — Not simply the last that he spoke, but the last which he spake by the spirit of God, assisting and directing him in an extraordinary manner. When we find death approaching, we should endeavour both to honour God, and to profit others with our last words. Let those who have had experience of God's goodness, and the pleasantness of the ways of wisdom, when they come to finish their course, leave a record of those experiences, and bear their testimony to the truth of the promise. Raised - Advanced from an obscure estate, to the kingdom. Whom, God singled out from all the families of Israel, and anointed to be king. Psalmist - He who was eminent among the people of God, for composing sweet and holy songs to the praise of God, and for the use of his church in after ages: these seem not to be the words of David, but of the sacred penman of this book.

His word — The following words, and consequently the other words and Psalms composed and uttered by me upon the like solemn occasions, are not to be looked upon as human inventions, but both the matter and the words of them are suggested by God's spirit, the great teacher of the church.

Rock — He who is the strength, and defense, and protector of his people; which he manifests by directing kings and rulers so to manage their power as may most conduce to their comfort and benefit. Ruleth - Here are the two principal parts of a king's duty, answerable to the two tables of God's law, justice towards men, and piety towards God, both which he is to maintain and promote among his people.

Shall be — These words are a farther description of the king's duty, which is not only to rule with justice and piety, but also with sweetness, and gentleness, and condescension to the infirmities of his people; to render his government as acceptable to them, as is the sun-shine in a clear morning, or the tender grass which springs out of the earth by the warm beams of the sun after the rain.

Altho' — Although God knows, that neither I, nor my children have lived and ruled as we should have done, so justly, and in the fear of the Lord; and therefore have not enjoyed that uninterrupted prosperity which we might have enjoyed. Covenant - Notwithstanding all our transgressions whereby we have broken covenant with God, yet God, to whom all my sins were known, was graciously pleased to make a sure covenant, to continue the kingdom to me, and to my seed forever, chap. vii, 16, until the coming of the Messiah who is to be my son and successor, and whose kingdom shall have no end. Ordered - Ordained in all points by God's eternal counsel; and disposed by his wise and powerful providence which will over-rule all things, even the sins of my house so far, that although he punished them for their sins, yet he will not utterly root them out, nor break his covenant made with me and mine. Sure - Or, preserved, by God's power and faithfulness in the midst of all oppositions. For this - Or, in this is, that is, it consists in, and depends upon this covenant. Salvation - Both mine own eternal salvation, and the preservation of the kingdom to me and mine. Tho' - Although God as yet hath not made my house or family to grow; that is, to increase, or to flourish with worldly glory as I expected; yet this is my comfort, that God will inviolably keep this covenant. But this refers also to the covenant of grace made with all believers. This is indeed an everlasting covenant, from everlasting, in the contrivance of it, and to everlasting, in the continuance and the consequence of it. It is ordered, well ordered in all things; admirably well, to advance the glory of God and the honour of the mediator, together with the holiness and happiness of believers. It is sure, and therefore sure, because well-ordered: the promised mercies are sure, on the performance of the conditions. It is all our salvation: nothing but this will save us, and this is sufficient. Therefore it should be all our desire. Let me have an interest in this covenant, and I have enough, I desire no more.

But — Having in the foregoing verses described the nature, and stability of that kingdom which God had by a sure covenant settled upon him and his seed; and especially, upon the Messiah, who was to be one of his posterity; he now describes the nature and miserable condition, of all the enemies of this holy and blessed kingdom. As thorns - Which men do not use to handle, but thrust them away. And so will God thrust away from himself, and from his people, and kingdom, all those who shall either secretly or openly set themselves against it.

Fenced — He must arm himself with some iron weapon, whereby he may cut them down; or, with the staff of a spear, or some such thing, whereby he may thrust them away from himself, that they do him no hurt. Burnt - Or, if they do not cut them down or thrust them away they will burn and consume them. The place - Or, in their place, where they grow or stand.

glossa.text:
*These however are.* ((HIERON.)) They are the last, because after the psalter and the other measures he is said to have composed this measure, in which he says: *David the son of Isai said: The man said, for whom a ladder was set up unto the Christ of the God of Jacob.* 

((RAB.)) Because they signify the last praise of confession, which, the enemy being overcome and the victory of death accomplished, the saints shall sing for ever.

*Excellent.* Because he prophesied most brilliantly of the Christ of God and of his incarnation and the redemption of the human race.

*In the fear.* He who exercises dominion over his subjects in the fear of God brings forth works of light illumined by the sun of justice, and nothing dark remains in them, but, watered by the shower of heavenly grace, living in the flesh he brings forth the shoots of the virtues as fruit.

*Nor is there.* ((RAB.)) He who meditates in the law of the Lord day and night becomes like a tree which, planted beside the waters, gives its fruit in its own time, and whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.

*And if any man.* He, that is, who, communicating in the sins of others because of the hardness of his heart, is pressed down by the weight of iniquities, and is pierced through with the darts of sins, and his works, worthy of eternal fires, shall be brought to nothing.

notes.text: Afflictions — All his sufferings for thy sake.
Until — Until I have raised an house in which the ark may be put.

It — Of the ark. Ephratah - In the tribe of Ephraim, which was called also Ephratah. Found it - Afterwards we found it in Kirjath- jearim, which signifies a city of woods, in the territory whereof the ark was seated for twenty years.
Tabernacles — Into his temple. Footstool - The ark, is often said to sit between the cherubim, which were above the ark.
Rest — Into thy resting place, the temple so called, Isaiah lxvi, 1, where thou hast now a fixed habitation. The ark - The seat of thy powerful and glorious presence.
David's sake — In regard of thy promises vouchsafed to David. Turn not - Cast me not out of thy presence. Of - Of me whom thou hast anointed to be king over thy people.

glossa.text:
*A canticle of degrees.* ((ID.)) In the thirteenth degree, now humble and meek, etc., *as far as* whence in Isaias: *Upon whom shall my Spirit rest, but upon the humble and the quiet, and him that trembleth at my words?* 

*Remember, O Lord, David, and all.* ((ID.)) First, showing the vow of building a house, he prays that he may fulfil it. Secondly, he shows the house built, there, *Behold, hear.* Thirdly, he tells the promises of God made to Sion when built, there, *The Lord hath sworn.* Willing therefore to build a house for the Lord, he says in the person of the whole Christ, the head: *O Lord,* etc. *David.* ((AUG.)) According to the letter, meek, in that he rendered not evil for evil to Saul.

*As he swore and vowed a vow.* That is, that he may fulfil what he promised: let no man presume to render by his own strength what he has vowed. And the Church has vowed in meekness that she may be the house of God, because nothing more pleasing can be offered to God. And it is a house if it seeks not its own, but rejoices in what is common: from things of one's own come evils, whence he says: *If I shall enter.* He knew that he was hindered by what was his own, lest a place for God should be made.

*If I shall enter* as far as *till I find out a place for the Lord.* The letter is left hanging, and it is an aposiopesis, as if he said: If I shall do this or that, let me never hereafter be believed. As it were, David swore to the Lord: *If I shall enter into the tabernacle of my house,* etc. ((CASS.)) Or, in the person of Christ, from that place: *If I shall enter into the tabernacle of my house,* namely of the heavenly habitation. The tabernacle is the heavenly habitation. *If I shall go up,* etc., to the right hand of the Father, where is the bed, that is, rest and the end of labours.

*Sleep* *Sumnum*, the rest of the three days' death. Then in other words he repeats the same. *And to my eyelids slumber. And rest to my temples* until the holy Church be founded by preaching. It is an aposiopesis, as it were, let me be believed no more.

*And to my eyelids.* ((AUG.)) There is he who sleeps not, but slumbers: now he is drawn back from earthly things, now he is rolled back into them, often he nods his head.

*And rest.* From the rest of the temples sleep comes to the eyes, because for them that are about to sleep the temples begin. When therefore something temporal begins to give delight unto sin, the temples are weighed down; but give not thyself to that delight, and sleep comes not to the eyes, by this thought, if, as though rubbing thy forehead, thou shakest off sleep.

*I shall find:* ((ID.)) he says it, because he sought long.

 *A place for the Lord:* he sought it in himself, who rests upon the humble and the quiet. And a man is a place of God if he forsakes his own things; or at the least, if he loves not himself, but God.

*A tabernacle.* ((ID.)) As yet we groan. In the house we shall praise, because groaning belongs to them that are on pilgrimage; praise to them that already abide in the fatherland. *To the God of Jacob.* He says that he has paid, as above he said that he had promised.

*Behold we have heard.* (CAS.) The second part, where the house is shown built, and where he also prays for those who are to be exalted, and that the Jews be not utterly strangers. *It in Ephrata,* ((AUG.)) or *it,* etc., *as far as* where were the brambles of idolatry.

((CASS.)) Behold, hear, namely that the Lord was to be born in Ephrata Bethlehem, where the Lord was born: it was heard that he should be born in Bethlehem, but for the faith of the Gentiles he was found *in the fields of the wood.*

*We will go in.* ((AUG.)) We too, by persevering in our warfare, have nevertheless gone in (or shall go in) into his tabernacle, the tabernacle of the God of Jacob: to this house belongs he who is framed together with others in charity as with living stones. He therefore enters who loves, and he who enters is made the house of God. *In the place.* The house of God is where he ought to be adored: apart from which God hears not unto life eternal. He belongs to the house who is framed together with others in charity. Or the place in which the feet of the house of the Lord stand is Christ, in whom they persevere.
*Arise.* ((ID.)) And it is said to him who says, *I have slept troubled:* Arise from death, into thy rest, that thou be troubled no more, because *death shall no more have dominion.*

*Priests.* ((ID.)) He takes the same men for priests and for saints, namely all the faithful. Or, by *priests* he signifies the prelates of the Church; by *saints,* the faithful that are subject. The ark therefore, which he had prayed might arise, he distinguishes by the parts of the Church.

*Priests,* as in the Old Testament the priests are adorned with divers ornaments, so the priests of the Gospel with divers virtues: these are the ornaments which God requires. For what the pontiffs of the law bore upon their garments, the priests of the Gospel ought to have in their hearts.

*For David the servant's sake.* ((CASS.)) *Remember:* And well do I say *for David's sake,* because *the Lord hath sworn to David.*

*For the sake of:* then in the person of David himself entreating God the Father.

((AUG.)) For because Christ turned away his face from the Jews unto the Gentiles, the Father is entreated for the remnant, that they may be saved, which was fulfilled in the apostles and in many others. And he says: *for David's sake,* as if he said: Remember me also, that for my sake thou cast not off the Jews utterly.

*He hath sworn.* ((CASS.)) The third part, where he tells the promises of God made to Sion when built, that is, to the Church. And David speaks in his own person or in the person of the whole Christ. *And he will not make it void* (otherwise) *he will not repent.* ((AUG.)) God is said to repent, etc., *as far as* for thou doest it because thou hadst erred: he does it, and delivers. *Of the fruit of thy womb.* He could have said, of the fruit of thy loins, etc., *as far as* because those whom David ruled temporally, Christ rules spiritually.

*If they shall keep.* ((ID.)) They seem to earn merit, etc., *as far as* this is not changed. *And their children.* ((CASS.)) *If they shall keep the testament. They shall sit upon thy seat,* that is, they shall be partakers of thy blessedness: that as thou art of kingly power, so they also, according to their measure, and this, *Unto the age of the age,* that is, unto eternity.

notes.text: John — The dedication of this book is contained in the fourth, fifth, and sixth verses; but the whole Revelation is a kind of letter. To the seven churches which are in Asia - That part of the Lesser Asia which was then a Roman province. There had been several other churches planted here; but it seems these were now the most eminent; and it was among these that St. John had laboured most during his abode in Asia. In these cities there were many Jews. Such of them as believed in each were joined with the gentile believers in one church. Grace be unto you, and peace - The favour of God, with all temporal and eternal blessings. From him who is, and who was, and who cometh, or, who is to come - A wonderful translation of the great name JEHOVAH: he was of old, he is now, he cometh; that is, will be forever. And from the seven spirits which are before his throne - Christ is he who "hath the seven spirits of God." "The seven lamps which burn before the throne are the seven spirits of God." " The lamb hath seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God." Seven was a sacred number in the Jewish church: but it did not always imply a precise number. It sometimes is to be taken figuratively, to denote completeness or perfection. By these seven spirits, not seven created angels, but the Holy Ghost is to be understood. The angels are never termed spirits in this book; and when all the angels stand up, while the four living creatures and the four and twenty elders worship him that sitteth on the throne, and the Lamb, the seven spirits neither stand up nor worship. To these "seven spirits of God," the seven churches, to whom the Spirit speaks so many things, are subordinate; as are also their angels, yea, and "the seven angels which stand before God." He is called the seven spirits, not with regard to his essence, which is one, but with regard to his manifold operations.

And from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the first begotten from the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth — Three glorious appellations are here given him, and in their proper order. He was the faithful witness of the whole will of God before his death, and in death, and remains such in glory. He rose from the dead, as "the first fruits of them that slept;" and now hath all power both in heaven and earth. He is here styled a prince: but by and by he hears his title of king; yea, King of kings, and Lord of lords." This phrase, the kings of the earth, signifies their power and multitude, and also the nature of their kingdom. It became the Divine Majesty to call them kings with a limitation; especially in this manifesto from his heavenly kingdom; for no creature, much less a sinful man, can bear the title of king in an absolute sense before the eyes of God.

To him that loveth us, and, out of that free, abundant love, hath washed us from the guilt and power of our sins with his own blood, and hath made us kings — Partakers of his present, and heirs of his eternal, kingdom. And priests unto his God and Father - To whom we continually offer ourselves, an holy, living sacrifice. To him be the glory - For his love and redemption. And the might - Whereby he governs all things.

Behold — In this and the next verse is the proposition, and the summary of the whole book. He cometh - Jesus Christ. Throughout this book, whenever it is said, He cometh, it means his glorious coming. The preparation for this began at the destruction of Jerusalem, and more particularly at the time of writing this book; and goes on, without any interruption, till that grand event is accomplished. Therefore it is never said in this book, He will come; but, He cometh. And yet it is not said, He cometh again: for when he came before, it was not like himself, but in "the form of a servant." But his appearing in glory is properly his coming; namely, in a manner worthy of the Son of God. And every eye - Of the Jews in particular. Shall see him - But with what different emotions, according as they had received or rejected him. And they who have pierced him - They, above all, who pierced his hands, or feet, or side. Thomas saw the print of these wounds even after his resurrection; and the same, undoubtedly, will be seen by all, when he cometh in the clouds of heaven. And all the tribes of the earth - The word tribes, in the Revelation, always means the Israelites: but where another word, such as nations or people, is joined with it, it implies likewise (as here) all the rest of mankind. Shall wail because of him - For terror and pain, if they did not wail before by true repentance. Yea, Amen - This refers to, every eye shall see him. He that cometh saith, Yea; he that testifies it, Amen. The word translated yea is Greek; Amen is Hebrew: for what is here spoken respects both Jew and gentile.

I am the Alpha and the Omega, saith the Lord God — Alpha is the first, Omega, the last, letter in the Greek alphabet. Let his enemies boast and rage ever so much in the intermediate time, yet the Lord God is both the Alpha, or beginning, and the Omega, or end, of all things. God is the beginning, as he is the Author and Creator of all things, and as he proposes, declares, and promises so great things: he is the end, as he brings all the things which are here revealed to a complete and glorious conclusion. Again, the beginning and end of a thing is in scripture styled the whole thing. Therefore God is the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end; that is, one who is all things, and always the same.

glossa.text: *To the seven churches.* He writes principally to those churches of Asia over which he had been set as master, and by likeness to the others. God gave to Christ, Christ to John, but John to the churches, or, through the seven, to the universal Church. Because *seven* signify universality, or because they are enlightened by the sevenfold Spirit. *In Asia.* Asia is a lifting up, the Church therefore is now in a lifting up of virtues, or once of vices. This Asia is not that great third part of the world, but a certain province where there were seven cities, and seven churches with seven bishops. *Grace be unto you.* He prepares his hearers in the salutation, and renders them well-disposed and attentive, as also in the prologue. *Who is and who was.* Eternally. But although he was born in time, he who once had been corruptible is now unchangeable through his humanity. Such is he to come, even if he does not appear such to the world. *And from the seven spirits, who in the sight. Spirit.* It sounds the same as charity. Whence to the Spirit is attributed the remission of sins, and the other gifts which are gifts of the whole Trinity, that we may understand the Trinity to work out of love alone. He is silent of the person of the Father, because concerning God the Creator no one had understood evil things, he sets down the person of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, concerning whom all heresies are born in the churches. *Thrones.* The thrones of God are his angels and holy men, in whom God now sits and judges, lest in time to come he judge.

*The faithful witness.* He says this because of those who despair of the death of Christ, as those who said: *We thought that it was he that should have redeemed Israel ((Luc. XXIV))*. *The firstborn of the dead.* As if he should say: Let it not terrify you, because he rose again, and is impassible. Or he is the first of those who mortify themselves, because he did no sin. *The prince of the kings of the earth.* The prince of the earthly powers, able to remove them, and, for the profit of his own or of the saints, permitting the ungodly to serve.
*And hath made us a kingdom to our God.* That is, powerful to resist vices, *and priests,* that is, offering our own selves to God for ourselves and for our brethren.

*Behold he cometh,* etc. And truly you ought to glorify him, because it is he who is to come to reward. *With the clouds,* that is, with the saints: because they were clouds in raining down doctrine upon others, and in working miracles; or, as he ascended in a cloud, so in a cloud will he come, by which we understand the clemency of God, whereby to the good there is refreshment and illumination, but to the evil terror and blinding. Which was also signified by the cloud whereby the children of Israel were led out of Egypt.

*And shall see him.* Another translation has: *All the earth shall see such a one.* As if he should say: Such shall they see him as the ungodly did not believe he would come. *Every eye.* The good shall see that they may rejoice, the evil that they may be confounded. *They shall bewail.* Or they shall dash themselves together over him, powerless to resist his command, after the likeness of a stone and of earthen vessels. Or *they shall bewail themselves,* that is, they shall grieve, looking back upon those who are founded upon him, because they shall not grieve so much over the torment itself, as that they shall be driven back from such fellowship.

*I am.* Truly he will come, because he himself promises that he will come. Or, the salutation being set first, he renders them attentive, as if he should say: Believe not this to have been said by me, but by Christ himself. *Alpha, the beginning.* Before whom is none, or from whom all things began. *Omega, the end.* After whom is none, or in whom all things shall be ended.

notes.text: My kingdom is not of this world — Is not an external, but a spiritual kingdom; that I might not be delivered to the Jews - Which Pilate had already attempted to do, ver. 31, and afterward actually did, chap. xix, 16.

Thou sayest — The truth. To this end was I born - Speaking of his human origin: his Divine was above Pilate's comprehension. Yet it is intimated in the following words, I came into the world, that I might witness to the truth - Which was both declared to the Jews, and in the process of his passion to the princes of the Gentiles also. Everyone that is of the truth - That is, a lover of it, heareth my voice - A universal maxim. Every sincere lover of truth will hear him, so as to understand and practice what he saith.

glossa.text: *Sayest thou this of thyself,* etc. Jesus knows what he himself asks and what the other will answer, but yet he willed it to be said, not that he might know, but that what he willed to know might be written.

*What hast thou done.* As if: If this be no fault, that thou hast called thyself king, what else hast thou done? As if: it is no wonder if thou art delivered to a judge to be punished, thou who callest thyself king. But if this were not the cause, then perhaps another must be sought; as if: confirm whether this be the cause which is objected, or another.

*A kingdom.* This is what he willed us to know; but first, by asking in his turn, he willed to show what was the opinion of men concerning his kingdom, of Jews or of Gentiles; and this being shown, he answers more fitly to both: *My kingdom is not of this world.* As if: ye are deceived; for I hinder not your dominion in this world, that ye may not vainly fear and be in servitude, but to come by believing to the heavenly kingdom.

*Thou sayest.* He fears not to confess himself a king, but it is so set free that he neither denies himself a king, nor confesses himself to be of the world, as he supposed who said: *Art thou a king then?* To whom he answered: *Thou sayest that I am a king.* As if he should say, being carnal thou speakest carnally.

notes.text: The thrones — The kingdoms of this world were destroyed by God the king, and judge of all, called the Ancient of days, because of his eternal deity.

Clothed — That majesty and strength which he always had, he will shew in the eyes of all people. Moved - He will overrule all the confusions in the world, so that they shall end in the erection of that kingdom of the Messiah, which can never be moved.
Floods — The enemies of thy kingdom.

Testimonies-Thy promises, which no less than the precepts are God's testimonies, or the witnesses, or declarations of his will to mankind. He seems here to speak of those precious promises concerning the erection of his kingdom in the world by the Messiah. Holiness — It becometh thy people to be holy in all their approach to thee. The danger and folly of persecuting the children of God, ver. 1-11. Assurance given to the persecuted, that God will deliver them, ver. 12-23.

glossa.text:
*The Lord hath reigned,* etc. ((CASS.)) The praise of Christ is sung here, etc., *as far as* from the praise of the house, there, *Thy house. Clothed with beauty.* ((AUG.)) Christ is beautiful in these things, etc., *as far as* the world which shall not be moved. *He hath put on beauty.* ((CASS.)) That is, comeliness, etc., *as far as* from the incarnation, when he taught men.

*He hath girded himself about.* He does not say, he girded, or he girded up, or he girded on, but he girded about. For we are girded when we are about to work, we are girded on when we are about to fight, we are girded up when we are about to go, we are girded about when we are about to minister. ((AUG.)) The girding therefore signifies works, etc., *as far as* because *better is he that overcometh anger than he that taketh a city. He hath girded himself about.* ((CASS.)) Ascending with the company of angels, or by strenuousness in working.

*For he hath established.* ((AUG.)) He has put on beauty and strength, that he might found the earth, whence he adds: *For he hath established.*

*From then.* ((ID.)) Or from that time; it marks the time of grace, and perhaps he understands this from the day before the sabbath, that is, in the sixth age of this world, in which the Lord came: but lest thou think that he then began, when he came born, he adds, *thou art from everlasting.*

*The floods have lifted up their voice.* ((AUG.)) Because the disciples, hearing, etc., *as far as* of the world, which began to be angry, or to persecute. *The floods have lifted up their waves,* etc. ((CASS.)) This is wanting in others, etc., *as far as* he who does all things well, he adds: *The Lord is wonderful on high.*

*Testimonies.* ((AUG.)) Because *the lifting up of the sea is wonderful,* etc., *as far as* and crowns out of the foretelling. ((CASS.)) *Testimonies.* Or thus, etc., *as far as* it contains, though in brief words.

Throughout this book, whenever it is said, He cometh, it means his glorious coming. The preparation for this began at the destruction of Jerusalem, and more particularly at the time of writing this book; and goes on, without any interruption, till that grand event is accomplished. Therefore it is never said in this book, He will come; but, He cometh. And yet it is not said, He cometh again: for when he came before, it was not like himself, but in "the form of a servant." But his appearing in glory is properly his coming; namely, in a manner worthy of the Son of God. And every eye - Of the Jews in particular. Shall see him - But with what different emotions, according as they had received or rejected him. And they who have pierced him - They, above all, who pierced his hands, or feet, or side. Thomas saw the print of these wounds even after his resurrection; and the same, undoubtedly, will be seen by all, when he cometh in the clouds of heaven. And all the tribes of the earth - The word tribes, in the Revelation, always means the Israelites: but where another word, such as nations or people, is joined with it, it implies likewise (as here) all the rest of mankind. Shall wail because of him - For terror and pain, if they did not wail before by true repentance. Yea, Amen - This refers to, every eye shall see him. He that cometh saith, Yea; he that testifies it, Amen. The word translated yea is Greek; Amen is Hebrew: for what is here spoken respects both Jew and gentile.

I am the Alpha and the Omega, saith the Lord God — Alpha is the first, Omega, the last, letter in the Greek alphabet. Let his enemies boast and rage ever so much in the intermediate time, yet the Lord God is both the Alpha, or beginning, and the Omega, or end, of all things. God is the beginning, as he is the Author and Creator of all things, and as he proposes, declares, and promises so great things: he is the end, as he brings all the things which are here revealed to a complete and glorious conclusion. Again, the beginning and end of a thing is in scripture styled the whole thing. Therefore God is the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end; that is, one who is all things, and always the same.

glossa.text: *To the seven churches.* He writes principally to those churches of Asia over which he had been set as master, and by likeness to the others. God gave to Christ, Christ to John, but John to the churches, or, through the seven, to the universal Church. Because *seven* signify universality, or because they are enlightened by the sevenfold Spirit. *In Asia.* Asia is a lifting up, the Church therefore is now in a lifting up of virtues, or once of vices. This Asia is not that great third part of the world, but a certain province where there were seven cities, and seven churches with seven bishops. *Grace be unto you.* He prepares his hearers in the salutation, and renders them well-disposed and attentive, as also in the prologue. *Who is and who was.* Eternally. But although he was born in time, he who once had been corruptible is now unchangeable through his humanity. Such is he to come, even if he does not appear such to the world. *And from the seven spirits, who in the sight. Spirit.* It sounds the same as charity. Whence to the Spirit is attributed the remission of sins, and the other gifts which are gifts of the whole Trinity, that we may understand the Trinity to work out of love alone. He is silent of the person of the Father, because concerning God the Creator no one had understood evil things, he sets down the person of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, concerning whom all heresies are born in the churches. *Thrones.* The thrones of God are his angels and holy men, in whom God now sits and judges, lest in time to come he judge.

*The faithful witness.* He says this because of those who despair of the death of Christ, as those who said: *We thought that it was he that should have redeemed Israel ((Luc. XXIV))*. *The firstborn of the dead.* As if he should say: Let it not terrify you, because he rose again, and is impassible. Or he is the first of those who mortify themselves, because he did no sin. *The prince of the kings of the earth.* The prince of the earthly powers, able to remove them, and, for the profit of his own or of the saints, permitting the ungodly to serve.
*And hath made us a kingdom to our God.* That is, powerful to resist vices, *and priests,* that is, offering our own selves to God for ourselves and for our brethren.

*Behold he cometh,* etc. And truly you ought to glorify him, because it is he who is to come to reward. *With the clouds,* that is, with the saints: because they were clouds in raining down doctrine upon others, and in working miracles; or, as he ascended in a cloud, so in a cloud will he come, by which we understand the clemency of God, whereby to the good there is refreshment and illumination, but to the evil terror and blinding. Which was also signified by the cloud whereby the children of Israel were led out of Egypt.

*And shall see him.* Another translation has: *All the earth shall see such a one.* As if he should say: Such shall they see him as the ungodly did not believe he would come. *Every eye.* The good shall see that they may rejoice, the evil that they may be confounded. *They shall bewail.* Or they shall dash themselves together over him, powerless to resist his command, after the likeness of a stone and of earthen vessels. Or *they shall bewail themselves,* that is, they shall grieve, looking back upon those who are founded upon him, because they shall not grieve so much over the torment itself, as that they shall be driven back from such fellowship.

*I am.* Truly he will come, because he himself promises that he will come. Or, the salutation being set first, he renders them attentive, as if he should say: Believe not this to have been said by me, but by Christ himself. *Alpha, the beginning.* Before whom is none, or from whom all things began. *Omega, the end.* After whom is none, or in whom all things shall be ended.

notes.text: My kingdom is not of this world — Is not an external, but a spiritual kingdom; that I might not be delivered to the Jews - Which Pilate had already attempted to do, ver. 31, and afterward actually did, chap. xix, 16.

Thou sayest — The truth. To this end was I born - Speaking of his human origin: his Divine was above Pilate's comprehension. Yet it is intimated in the following words, I came into the world, that I might witness to the truth - Which was both declared to the Jews, and in the process of his passion to the princes of the Gentiles also. Everyone that is of the truth - That is, a lover of it, heareth my voice - A universal maxim. Every sincere lover of truth will hear him, so as to understand and practice what he saith.

glossa.text: *Sayest thou this of thyself,* etc. Jesus knows what he himself asks and what the other will answer, but yet he willed it to be said, not that he might know, but that what he willed to know might be written.

*What hast thou done.* As if: If this be no fault, that thou hast called thyself king, what else hast thou done? As if: it is no wonder if thou art delivered to a judge to be punished, thou who callest thyself king. But if this were not the cause, then perhaps another must be sought; as if: confirm whether this be the cause which is objected, or another.

*A kingdom.* This is what he willed us to know; but first, by asking in his turn, he willed to show what was the opinion of men concerning his kingdom, of Jews or of Gentiles; and this being shown, he answers more fitly to both: *My kingdom is not of this world.* As if: ye are deceived; for I hinder not your dominion in this world, that ye may not vainly fear and be in servitude, but to come by believing to the heavenly kingdom.

*Thou sayest.* He fears not to confess himself a king, but it is so set free that he neither denies himself a king, nor confesses himself to be of the world, as he supposed who said: *Art thou a king then?* To whom he answered: *Thou sayest that I am a king.* As if he should say, being carnal thou speakest carnally.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Are you a king? Pilate asked.
My kingdom is not from this world.
The Lord reigns, robed in majesty;
his throne is established from of old.
To the Ancient of Days came one like a son of man,
and to him was given dominion that shall not pass away.
Come, let us worship the ruler of the kings of earth.
Jesus Christ is Lord. Amen.

lines: Pilate asked, So you are a king? And Jesus answered, For this I was born, and for this I came into the world: to testify to the truth.
Jesus Christ is Lord, the King of kings.
The Lord reigns, robed in majesty, girded with strength; the world is established and shall never be moved.
Jesus Christ is Lord, the King of kings.
He is the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead, the ruler of the kings of the earth.
Jesus Christ is Lord, the King of kings.
Look, he is coming with the clouds, and his dominion is everlasting. Lift up your heads and worship the King.
Jesus Christ is Lord, the King of kings. Amen.
